best.hypothesis: The best parent (c011/c018 lineage) already clamps momentum decay to 0.5 and caps per-net weight; the remaining TNS lever inside `update_net_weights` is the *degree threshold* used to ignore high-fanout nets — lowering the effective `ignore_net_degree` cap so that moderate-fanout nets (which carry many moderate violations) also receive timing weight, while still skipping true clock/reset high-fanout nets, should spread repair effort and reduce TNS broadly.
best.analysis: Hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with dTNS gains (+28–45%) exceeding dWNS (+24–26%), consistent with spreading repair to moderate-fanout nets. bp-ng45 and ariane133-ng45 moved most; bp_fe-ng45 least, plausibly because its violation mix is dominated by true high-fanout nets still skipped. Overflow ~120–135 is stable, so no legality concern. Next step: sweep the effective `ignore_net_degree` cap (e.g., 200/150/100) to find where moderate-fanout weighting saturates before clock/reset nets leak in, and confirm TNS gains persist without overflow regression.
best.expected: TNS improves on all three cases (main effect), WNS roughly neutral to slightly better, overflow unchanged, runtime unchanged.
